_note: The Hole Truth, the colony's monthly newsletter (#424). The sim keeps the month's facts (src/sim/newsletter.ts): keep is how many back issues a hole holds, maxOutcomes how many event outcomes an issue reprints, grumblePoints and praisePoints how many happiness points a cause must cost (or give) before a notable grumbles (or praises) it. The words are src/view/newsletter.ts's: each story is a list of templates, one picked by the issue's dice. Placeholders: {hole} the hole's name, {n} a count, {N} a count in words, {name} a notable, {role} their job, {trait} one of their traits, {baby} a newborn's first name and {family} a family name (both from data/notables.json), {room} a room's name, {rooms} a list of them, {floor} the deepest floor, {milestone} a milestone's title, {find} what the drill struck (from `finds`, by event id), {pop} the population, {happy} the average happiness. Headlines come from the month's biggest story, in the order of `order`. Voice (docs/ART.md, Voice): warm, dry, a pun allowed, never at the player's expense.
name: The Hole Truth
tagline: All the news that fits the shaft

head: It's a Martian!
{hole} welcomes its first native
First cry heard below the surface
text: {baby} {family} arrived this month, the first person ever born in {hole}. Both parents report the delivery was 'mostly gravity-assisted.' Children don't work, but they will want a school.
Meet {baby} {family}, {hole}'s first child born on Mars. The clinic staff have already been asked about the view upstairs. A school will be wanted before long.

head: Small arrivals
The nursery fills up
More little Martians
one: Welcome to {baby} {family}, born this month. The clinic reports one tired but very happy family.
{baby} {family} joined us this month, weighing in at about a third of what they'd weigh on Earth.
many: {N} children were born this month, among them {baby} {family}. The clinic asks that everyone please stop asking the newborns about their career plans.
A busy month at the clinic: {N} births, including little {baby} {family}. Lullabies may be heard through the corridors at odd hours.

head: Fresh faces in the corridors
New neighbours
The welcome mat gets dusty
text: {N} new colonists settled in this month. If you see someone staring at the shaft for a long time, they're new. Say hello.
{N} newcomers joined {hole}. They've been shown the galley, the restrooms and which elevator sticks, in that order.
We welcome {N} new neighbours. They report the trip was long, the landing bumpy and the welcome warm.

head: We remember
Fond farewells
text: {N} of our elders passed away this month. They helped dig the place we live in, and they'll be missed.
This month we said goodbye to {N} of our elders. Raise a cup to them at the galley tonight.

head: Grown up and clocking in
Fresh hands on the job
text: {N} of our children came of age this month and joined the workforce. Their first complaint about the shift roster is expected any day now.
{N} young Martians grew up this month. They've never seen a blue sky and they don't seem to mind.

head: Deeper we go
The drill digs in
Floor {floor}, going down
text: The drill finished {N} new floor this month: {hole} now goes down {floor} floors. Elevator music remains under review.
{hole} is now {floor} floors deep. The drill crew would like it noted that they're not boring, they're boring.
many: The drill finished {N} new floors this month: {hole} now goes down {floor} floors. Elevator music remains under review.

head: Ribbon cutting
New doors open
Fresh paint on the rock
one: A new {room} opened its doors this month. Early reviews are positive, if you don't count the smell of fresh sealant.
The crews finished a new {room} this month, on time and only a little dusty.
many: The crews finished {N} rooms this month: {rooms}. Somewhere, a foreman is finally sitting down.
{N} rooms opened this month: {rooms}. The hole is getting roomier, so to speak.

head: The drill strikes {find}
Something down there
A find on floor {floor}
text: The drill struck {find} this month. The crew have filed their report and are already arguing about what to name it.
News from the bottom of the hole: the drill hit {find}. The scientists are thrilled; the drill crew are just glad it wasn't their lunchbox.

head: {milestone}!
A milestone for {hole}
text: {hole} reached a milestone this month: {milestone}. Someone suggested a party. Someone always does.
Mark your calendars: this month {hole} reached {milestone}. The deputy has asked for it to be written down somewhere permanent, so here it is.

head: Party in the hole
A feast below the dust
{hole} celebrates
text: The festival went off with a bang (the good kind). Turnout was excellent and the meals ran out at exactly the right moment.
This month's festival was a hit. Work slowed for a day, smiles didn't. Leftovers are, as ever, a myth.

head: Dust gets in everywhere
Storm passes over
text: A dust storm blew through this month. The solar arrays sulked, the batteries held, and the airlocks are still finding grit.
Weather report: dusty, then dustier, then fine. The storm's gone, but check your boots.

head: A new name to know
text: {name} joined the colony this month and is already making themselves known. Watch this space.

head: A quiet month in {hole}
Nothing to report (and that's good news)
Steady as she digs
text: Nothing much happened this month, which on Mars is exactly what you want. {pop} people, all still breathing.
A quiet month. The air held, the lights stayed on and nobody fell down the shaft. We call that a win.
Slow news month. The editor considered running a story about the new mop in the galley, but decided against it.

noise: "I can hear the machinery through my pillow. I'd like a quieter neighbour, or a thicker wall, or both."
smell: "Something smells, and it isn't me. Could someone shut a door between us and wherever that's coming from?"
crowding: "I share my home with more people than I've met. A few more homes, please."
homeless: "Some of us are sleeping in the corridors. It's a lovely corridor. It's not a bed."
airQuality: "The air's stale where I live. I don't need much, just air that hasn't been breathed already."
variety: "Same meal again. I'm not complaining. I'm noting it, for the record, loudly."
noSeat: "There's nowhere to sit at mealtimes. I eat standing up like a horse."
noRestroom: "The nearest restroom is a long walk. A long, urgent walk."
temperature: "Is it me, or is it cold enough down here to keep the milk fresh? I don't have any milk."
noClinic: "If I sprain an ankle, where do I go? Asking for a friend. The friend is my ankle."
schooling: "The kids need a school. I love them, but they've started teaching each other."
elderCare: "Our elders deserve somewhere comfortable to spend their days."
grief: "We have nowhere to lay our dead to rest. It weighs on all of us."
homeWear: "My home's seen better days. So have I, but I can't be repaired by a maintenance crew."
sharedWear: "The common rooms are getting shabby. A bit of upkeep wouldn't go amiss."
holeHealth: "People are feeling poorly. I think it's the water, or the meals, or both. Someone should look."

default: "Things could be better around here. I'm not saying how. I'm saying they could."

windows: "I've got a window on the shaft. I could watch the dust settle all day, and some days I do."
amenityComfort: "The park's lovely this time of year. Every time of year, actually. There aren't seasons down here."
amenityHealth: "Went to the gym. Felt great. Will never shut up about it."
neighbourComfort: "Good neighbours make a good hole. Ours are great."
ownComfort: "I like my home. It's warm, it's mine, and the rock doesn't talk back."
lining: "Whoever finished my walls did a lovely job. I'd tip them if we had money."
sharedLining: "The common rooms look smart these days. Somebody's been busy."
temperature: "Nice and toasty down here. Mars can keep its weather."

finds.ore_vein: a rich vein of iron ore
finds.microfossils: microfossils, the traces of something that lived here once

fillers: Lost: one left glove, near the airlock. Answers to 'glove'.
Reminder: the shaft is not a rubbish chute. It is a very long way down, and someone has to fetch it.
The galley reports that Tuesday's mystery stew has been solved. It was beans.
Found: one wrench, slightly scorched. Owner may collect from the workshop, and explain.
For trade: one Earth novel, read eleven times. Ending still sad.
Wanted: a name for the drill. 'The Drill' has been ruled out as 'unimaginative' by the drill crew.
Reminder from maintenance: please don't lick the condensation.
This month's sunrise was rated four stars by the people with windows. Everyone else has to take their word for it.
Gravity remains at 38%. Please continue to enjoy it responsibly.
The elevator suggestion box is full. Please stop suggesting stairs.
sign: Keep your boots dusted and your hatches shut.
See you next month, same hole, same time.
